assessment:
Two wishes now, and they are not the same tool. Vampiric Tutor is {B} at instant speed for any card, taken in secret, put on top, costing two life and your next draw. Forerunner of the Legion is a {2}{W} 2/2 that finds a Vampire, REVEALS it, and puts it on top — and being a Vampire spell, casting it mints an eminence token on the way in.

Start with what Forerunner cannot do, because it decides which wish goes where. THE GO-WIDE KILL wants a payoff that converts the eminence tokens into damage beside a card that multiplies them. Six cards do the converting — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight, Witty Roastmaster, Mirkwood Bats — and not one of them is a Vampire, so Forerunner finds NONE of the kill's payoff leg. The other half of that pair holds three true doublers — Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Elspeth — and four cards that simply make extra tokens. Forerunner finds none of the doublers and three of the makers: Mavren Fein, Charismatic Conqueror, Bloodline Keeper. Stack 010 is the reason that gap is worth naming: three doublers turn one eminence trigger into eight tokens under all six application orders, and Forerunner cannot go and get the third one.

So the go-wide kill is Vampiric Tutor's job. It assembles in 44.5% of games and by turn six in 28.5%; spend the wish on it and that is 52.0% and 34.3%, mean turn 5.043 (◆ goldfish, 10,000 seeded games). Its third leg — a Vampire cheap enough to cast alongside the rest of the turn — is already there in 92.3% of games and 84.8% by turn six, so never spend a wish on it.

Mirkwood Bats is the newest card in that leg and the one to know before you point a wish anywhere. Stack 011 is checker-passed that it triggers once per TOKEN created, not once per creation event, with the count following the tokens in the final modified event — a doubler that makes two tokens makes two drains. It is also the only one of the six keyed on creation rather than on a creature entering, which cuts both ways: it drains again when you sacrifice a token and it sees Voldaren Epicure's Blood token, and it does nothing when the Vampire you cast enters. One trap from the same stack: if the Bats drain is the first life loss of the turn, the tokens that caused it do not enter with Vampire Socialite's counter, though the Vampire spell resolving afterwards does.

Forerunner's job is the drain lines, the bodies, and the deck's second line. Both single points of failure are Vampires: Bloodthirsty Conqueror, half of the checker-passed loops in stacks 004 and 006, and Bloodletter of Aclazotz, the doubler in stack 003. So are Vito, Sanctum Seeker, Champion of Dusk. It also reaches the whole of the drain that fires when a creature DIES: Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, two cards, drawn in 30.4% of games and 24.1% by turn six — a line you can run rather than one you wait to have done to you, because Indulgent Aristocrat's {2} sacrifice carries no tap symbol and Skullclamp's +1/-1 makes a 1/1 token a 2/0 for a {1} equip and draws two. Sanguine Bond and Throne of the God-Pharaoh are not Vampires, and this search will never see them.

Two costs to say out loud before either wish. Both put the card on TOP, which is a turn of delay unless something cashes it — Herald's Horn's upkeep look hands you a Vampire creature and leaves your draw step intact, and Skullclamp, Night's Whisper, Welcoming Vampire, Caretaker's Talent, Preacher of the Schism, Champion of Dusk and Pact of the Serpent all turn a stacked top card into a card in hand. And Forerunner reveals what it takes: the blue seat learns your plan a full turn before you cast it. In the one game on record, two counters on two named cards decided the result. Vampiric Tutor reveals nothing, and that is a reason to hold it for the turn the table is representing an answer.

tutors.notes: One mana at instant speed, any card, on TOP — plus two life and your next draw. That shape dictates the timing: cast it at the end step right before your untap, when the table's mana and attention are spent, and only when you will cast the card the turn it arrives. A Vampiric cast three turns early is a card spent arranging a draw you then draw into removal range. Pay the two life without blinking — Sanctum Seeker and the lifegain halves hand it straight back. It is also the only one of the two wishes that reaches a card which is not a Vampire, so spend it on the enchantments, the artifact and the payoffs — Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Mirkwood Bats, Sanguine Bond, Throne of the God-Pharaoh — and leave the Vampires to Forerunner. That now includes the two drains that fire when a creature DIES: Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant are their own component, they are both Vampires, and Forerunner reaches them for three mana and a body. And it takes in secret: nothing is revealed, which is what makes it the wish to cast against a seat holding counterspells.

targets.scenario: Opponent 3's end step, turn four. You have a doubler and five bodies but no converter, three untapped lands, and your untap is next. Player 2 just tapped out for a planeswalker.
targets.why: The go-wide kill is online by turn six in 28.5% of your games on natural draws and 34.3% with a wish spent on it — this is the wish, at the moment the table cannot answer it. Roastmaster is one of SIX cards that turn the eminence tokens into damage — five when a creature ENTERS, and Mirkwood Bats when a token is CREATED — and not one of the six is a Vampire, so Forerunner cannot go and get any of them. This half of the plan is Vampiric Tutor's alone. Roastmaster is the converter on a body: every later entry is one damage to each seat, and he triggers the other converters on his own way in. One mana at their end step, cast him on your turn with mana to spare.

citations.quote: prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent

targets.scenario: Turn five. Anointed Procession has been down since turn three and Mondrak, Glory Dominus resolved last turn, so two doublers are live. You hold two cheap Vampires and no payoff has come — a payoff is drawn in 67.4% of games and by turn six in 56.7%, so this is the third of games that has to go and get one. Opponent 3 is on 14 and tapped out.
targets.why: With two doublers already down, take the payoff that pays per TOKEN. Stack 011 is checker-passed on the count: Bats triggers once per token created, not once per creation event, and the number follows the tokens in the final modified event — one doubler turns an eminence trigger into two tokens and two drains, two doublers into four and four. Handle the bigger board honestly rather than quoting it: stack 010 proves three doublers make eight tokens from one trigger, but that board holds no Bats, so eight drains is two proofs composed and not a board anyone has resolved. Why this and not Witty Roastmaster, which the same wish also buys — Bats keys on creation, so it drains AGAIN when you sacrifice a token, and it sees Voldaren Epicure's Blood token, which nothing waiting for a creature to enter ever will. What it does not do is fire when the Vampire you cast enters; Roastmaster does. With doublers down, buy Bats. With none, buy Roastmaster. One trap in the line you just bought, from the same stack: if the Bats drain is the first life loss of the turn, the tokens that caused it do NOT enter with Vampire Socialite's +1/+1 counter — when they enter the ability has only triggered, and it cannot reach back. The Vampire spell resolving afterwards does get it.

citations.quote: reach must scale (each-opponent drains, commander damage, damage doublers)

targets.scenario: Sanctum Seeker and six other Vampires are on your board, untapped, and your attack is next turn. Two opponents are at 14 and 16. You can pay {B}{B}{B} plus one.
targets.why: This is the closing fetch, and the maths is verified: stack 003 resolves a seven-Vampire attack with Bloodletter and Sanctum Seeker as 14 life off each opponent on attack declaration alone — before a single point of combat damage. Both life totals in this scenario are inside that number. The rule attached: he is the only triple-black cast in the 99, so confirm the {B}{B}{B} is actually there before the wish, not after — black is 30 sources against the 36 a 90% on-curve rate would take.

targets.scenario: The wish nobody sees coming. Opponent 2's end step. The blue seat has held two untapped Islands for three turns and has countered the last two spells anyone tried to resolve. Edgar is on the battlefield, you have six Vampires, a five-mana refuel stranded in hand, and one black source untapped.
targets.why: Do not fetch a better spell. Fetch the thing that makes the spell you are already holding resolve. Deflecting Swat changes the target of a counterspell, and with Edgar on the battlefield you cast it without paying its mana cost — so the refuel goes through and their held mana bought a redirected spell. Read the condition rather than the card: 'if you control a commander' means Edgar on the battlefield, not in the command zone, and without him the Swat costs {2}{R} and belongs to a different turn. Vampiric Tutor reveals nothing on its way through, so the seat you are answering cannot see the answer coming. In the one game on record, two counters on named cards decided the result.

citations.quote: sequence so one removal spell can't break the chain

tutors.notes: {2}{W} for a 2/2, and three things happen on one cast. It is a Vampire spell, so eminence mints a 1/1 token — stack 010 is checker-passed that eminence works with Edgar in the command zone and never on the battlefield. The body arrives. And its enter trigger searches out a Vampire card and puts it on top. White is 22 sources against a 22-source yardstick, so unlike the deck's black costs it casts on curve. Two limits govern every fetch below and neither goes away. The search is Vampire-only, and that cuts along the deck's main plan rather than across it: of the SIX cards that turn the eminence tokens into damage — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight, Witty Roastmaster, Mirkwood Bats — it can find NONE, and of the seven cards in the multiplier-or-extra-token-maker group it can find three — Mavren Fein, Charismatic Conqueror, Bloodline Keeper — every one of which makes an extra token rather than doubling one. The three that actually double (Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Elspeth) are all out of reach. What it does reach whole is the deck's second line — Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, the two drains that fire when a creature dies — and every Vampire the drain lines are built from. And it REVEALS what it takes, so the table sees the card a full turn before you cast it. Fetch what you want NEXT turn, not this one — unless Herald's Horn is out with Vampire named, in which case the upkeep look puts the card in hand and your draw step still draws. Its second ability is small and real: every later Vampire that enters, tokens included, pumps a creature of your choice until end of turn.

targets.scenario: Turn three, Forerunner is the play. You have two bodies — which is where the goldfish has you on turn three, mean 2.058 — no converter on the battlefield, and all three opponents untapped and above 30.
targets.why: Buy the conversion Forerunner can actually reach. Every one of the six cards that turns a token into damage is outside it: Purphoros is a God, Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call are enchantments, Corpse Knight is a Zombie, Witty Roastmaster a Devil, and Mirkwood Bats a Bat. The two drains it CAN see, Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, fire when a creature dies — a real second line, and not the one stack 009 kills from. What is left is combat, and Sanctum Seeker is the card that turns width into damage there: each attacking Vampire drains every opponent for one. Stack 003 measured that at width — seven attackers is seven triggers, and with Bloodletter of Aclazotz out it is 14 life off each opponent on attack declaration, before blockers are declared. The life it hands back is also the input Vito and Sanguine Bond convert.

citations.quote: Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game

targets.scenario: The behind fetch. Turn five or six and the first line has not arrived: no payoff drawn, one doubler down doing nothing, Indulgent Aristocrat on the battlefield beside three eminence tokens. Two opponents are inside 20.
targets.why: Switch lines rather than waiting for the one that did not come. The deck's second drain fires when a creature DIES, it is two cards — Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant — and both are Vampires, so this is the one component Forerunner reaches whole. It is drawn in only 30.4% of games and 24.1% by turn six, which is exactly what a search is for. With Celebrant down, every creature you lose drains each opponent for one and pays you one, so the sweeper the table is holding costs them the game instead of costing you yours — and you rebuild from the command zone. Prefer him over Blood Artist when the whole table matters: Artist drains one target player per death, Celebrant hits everyone. The half worth correcting: this is not a line you sit and wait to have done to you. Indulgent Aristocrat's {2}, sacrifice a creature carries no tap symbol, so it runs the turn it lands and as often as you can pay, and Skullclamp's +1/-1 makes a 1/1 token a 2/0 for a {1} equip and draws two on the way out. With Mirkwood Bats also down, one sacrificed token pays twice: Bats on the sacrifice, Celebrant on the death.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can

targets.scenario: The closing fetch. Turn six or later. Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose is on the battlefield and untouched, you have five lands untapped after Forerunner, and nobody at the table has shown blue mana this game.
targets.why: The one fetch that ends the game instead of improving it. Stack 004 is checker-passed: Conqueror beside Vito is a deterministic table kill from a three-life seed — 13 Vito resolutions, both opponents to exactly zero, and the loop consumes no cards, mana or creatures. Stack 006 proves the same pairing with Sanguine Bond in Vito's place, and Forerunner can find the Conqueror half and the Vito half and never Sanguine Bond, which is an enchantment. Price two things before you take it. He costs {3}{B}{B} and lands the turn AFTER the search, and he is a 5/5 creature, so every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed creature removal — stack 004 names that cost itself. Then there is the reveal, which tells the table which card is coming while it is still on top of your library. The loop assembles in 4.6% of games and 10.2% with a wish, so carry the ticket and never steer for it.

targets.scenario: The wish nobody sees coming. Turn three. Bloodletter of Aclazotz and Champion of Dusk are both in hand, your three lands produce exactly one black between them, and a spare eminence token is on the battlefield.
targets.why: Fetch the mana, not the threat. Master of Dark Rites is a one-mana 1/1 that taps and sacrifices another creature for {B}{B}{B}, and eminence prints the creature to sacrifice on every Vampire spell you cast. Black is 30 sources against the 36 a 90% on-curve rate would take, and Bloodletter of Aclazotz is the only triple-black cast in the 99, so this is the card that makes the deck's most expensive coloured cost payable a turn early. The restriction is exact, and deck-facts names it: that mana pays for Vampire, Cleric and Demon SPELLS, and an activated ability is not a spell. It casts Bloodletter (Vampire Demon), Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Champion of Dusk (Vampire Knights) and Vito (Vampire Cleric); it cannot pay Vito's own {3}{B}{B} lifelink activation or Indulgent Aristocrat's {2}, and Sanguine Bond is an enchantment and out of reach. Bank the free part, which got bigger with stack 011: the token you sacrifice is BOTH a token sacrificed and a creature dying, so Mirkwood Bats, Cruel Celebrant, Blood Artist and Cordial Vampire all fire off one activation cost.

gaps: The goldfish models only UNRESTRICTED tutors as wildcards ('search your library for a card'), so every *_assisted figure quoted here is Vampiric Tutor alone. Forerunner of the Legion is priced at zero in every measurement of this deck — goldfish_targets.json says so in its own note, and the model has no way to represent a Vampire-only search. The assisted figures are therefore a ceiling on Vampiric Tutor (its top-of-library lag and two life are not modelled) and a floor on the pair.

Stack 011 proves the per-token count on a board holding ONE doubler and two tokens. The eight-token figure is stack 010's, on a board that holds no Mirkwood Bats — so eight drains from one eminence trigger is those two proofs composed, and this guide says so wherever it is quoted rather than treating it as a resolved board.

The declaration's label for the kill's payoff leg reads 'fires when a token is CREATED', and five of its six members in fact key on a creature ENTERING; only Mirkwood Bats keys on creation. The component is right — a doubled eminence token is both created and entering, so all six fire — but the two events come apart on a SACRIFICED token and on a noncreature token, and this guide distinguishes them by card rather than by the label.

Nothing simulates opposing interaction, so every fetch-versus-hold call here — and the whole cost of Forerunner's reveal — is coaching judgment on top of measured assembly rates. The one logged game had two named cards countered by the same seat; one game is an anecdote, not a rate, and no artifact measures what a revealed fetch costs.

There is no graveyard answer in the 99 to fetch: confirmed at the oracle level across all 96 entries, where the only cards naming a graveyard are Takenuma, Abandoned Mire (your own) and Nighthawk Scavenger (a power count). Against a reanimator seat these two tutors buy speed, never an answer. A tutor cannot buy a class the deck does not hold.
